title: Maximum Subarray
keyIdea: Kadane's: walk once with a running sum. Record it whenever it beats the best so far. If it drops below 0, reset it to 0: a negative prefix can only make any subarray that continues from it smaller, so the next subarray should start fresh.

approaches.name: Extreme brute force
approaches.idea: Your commented version: for every start i and end j, add nums[i..j] again from scratch.
approaches.why: n² pairs, each summed in up to n steps.

approaches.name: Better: two loops
approaches.idea: Your commented version: for each start i, extend j and keep a running sum, so each subarray costs O(1).

approaches.name: Kadane's algorithm
approaches.idea: Your active code: sum += nums[i]; maxi = max(maxi, sum); if sum < 0, sum = 0.

quiz.q: Why reset sum to 0 when it goes negative?
options: A negative prefix only lowers any subarray that continues from it, so starting fresh is never worse
Because the answer is never negative

quiz.q: Why start maxi at INT_MIN instead of 0?
options: If every number is negative, the answer is the largest (still negative) number

quiz.q: Why update maxi before the sum < 0 check?
options: So a single negative number can still be recorded as the answer
